chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Fadala from Husayn from Ibn Muskhan from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad Al-Sayqali, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When a man prays sitting while he is able to stand, he should double (the number of rak'ahs).' And that which clarifies that this is only obligatory for one with this description is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who prays sitting while able to stand?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a person praying while sitting despite having the physical ability to stand must double their rak'ahs to compensate for the diminished reward of the sitting posture. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that voluntary sitting during obligatory prayer reduces the spiritual merit, necessitating a quantitative increase in prostrations to achieve equivalence with standing. The text serves as a precursor to further clarifications regarding the specific conditions under which this doubling is obligatory versus merely recommended.
